summary: This is the RobotPet class re-implemented with three species subclasses — RobotCat, RobotBird, and RobotDog — each overriding show_talent to describe its own trick. Nothing is printed yet; this file is the new feature that the next step will cover with unit tests.

lines.text: The setter guards the battery level so it can never leave the 0–100 range, which is exactly the kind of boundary rule worth pinning down with a unit test.
Charging assigns through the property rather than touching self._battery, so the clamping rule applies here too and charging past 100 quietly stops at 100.

lines.code:
def show_talent(self):
        return f"{self.name} performs a generic trick!"
lines.text: The base class supplies a fallback talent, so a plain RobotPet still works while each subclass replaces this with something specific.
Each subclass declares RobotPet as its parent and defines nothing but show_talent, inheriting the constructor, the battery property, and charge unchanged.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} catches a frisbee in mid-air!"
lines.text: Because every subclass returns its message instead of printing it, a test can call show_talent and compare the returned string directly.
